name: release
description: The release workflow a repository's merge master runs: merge window -> QA gauntlet -> ship staging -> soak -> ship production. Kanna binds it when it claims the merge master through a merge handoff or a merge signal; it is never created by name. Every transition is manual: the gauntlet and the soak are stages without a role that park for a person, and no stage prompt authorizes a publish, so the ship agent reports what would ship unless a person authorizes an operation in its session.

stages.name: in progress
stages.description: Merge window: the merge master takes reviewed pull requests as handoffs arrive and merges what the repository's policy accepts. It keeps the stage name every merge master has run under, so a live merge master moves onto this workflow without renaming its stage.

stages.name: qa gauntlet
stages.description: The window's merges go through the repository's long-running verification. A repository adds the setup that starts it; a person advances once it has passed.

stages.name: ship staging
stages.description: The shipping agent reports what would ship to staging through the repository's declared release procedure.
stages.prompt: Programmatic mode. Report what would ship to staging from the work this release's merge window merged: use only the repository's declared read-only status and dry-run surfaces, then record your result. This prompt authorizes no publish, deployment, rollback or release-branch change; a person who wants one asks for it in this session.

stages.name: soak
stages.description: Staging soaks for the period the repository's release procedure sets. Kanna runs no timer; a person advances when the soak is over.

stages.name: ship production
stages.description: The shipping agent reports what a production promotion of the soaked release would ship.
stages.prompt: Programmatic mode. Report what a production promotion of the soaked staging release would ship: use only the repository's declared read-only status and dry-run surfaces, then record your result. This prompt authorizes no production operation; production requires the request of a named human in this session, as your definition says.
